## Welcome

This site is a guided tour of the Kaggle
[**Housing Prices Competition for Kaggle Learn Users**](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/home-data-for-ml-course)
— the Ames, Iowa house-price dataset — worked end to end in R with the
[tidymodels](https://www.tidymodels.org/) framework. It is written for an R user
who is comfortable with the language and with statistics, but is **new to
Kaggle** — so we narrate the *competition workflow* as well as the modelling
reasoning, and we lean on `ggplot2` for every chart.

It is the regression companion to the classification-flavoured
[Titanic tour](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/titanic): same structure,
same tidymodels muscle memory, different problem shape.

### What is this competition?

- You get a **training set** (`data/raw/train.csv`, 1460 houses) where the
  outcome is known: the **`SalePrice`** in dollars.
- You get a **test set** (`data/raw/test.csv`, 1459 houses) with the *same 79
  features but no `SalePrice`*.
- Your job: **predict `SalePrice` for every test house**, write those
  predictions to a CSV (`Id,SalePrice`), and upload it. Kaggle scores your CSV
  and places you on the leaderboard.

::: {.callout-tip}
## The metric shapes everything
Submissions are scored on **Root-Mean-Squared-Error between the logarithm of the
predicted and the logarithm of the observed SalePrice**. Taking logs means an
error on a cheap house counts as much as a proportional error on an expensive
one. So throughout this project **we model `log(SalePrice)`** — which makes each
model's cross-validated `rmse` directly comparable to the leaderboard score.
:::

## The goal

Predict `SalePrice` for the 1459 test houses as accurately as possible (lowest
log-RMSE), and document the reasoning so the whole thing is reproducible and
teachable.

We fit **six** different model families on identical features so they can be
compared apples-to-apples, then blend them in a stacked ensemble:

| Model | Engine | Why it's interesting |
|-------|--------|----------------------|
| [XGBoost](docs/02-xgboost.qmd) | `xgboost` | Gradient-boosted trees — the Kaggle workhorse |
| [Random Forest](docs/03-random-forest.qmd) | `ranger` | Bagged trees — robust, low-tuning baseline |
| [Neural Net](docs/04-neural-net.qmd) | `nnet` | A small MLP — needs normalized inputs |
| [Elastic Net](docs/06-elasticnet.qmd) | `glmnet` | Penalised linear baseline — interpretable |
| [SVM (RBF)](docs/07-svm.qmd) | `kernlab` | Nonlinear kernel surface — diverse errors |
| [MARS](docs/08-mars.qmd) | `earth` | Piecewise-linear splines — nonlinear, interpretable |
| [Stacked Ensemble](docs/05-stack.qmd) | `stacks` | Learns a blend over all of the above |

## How the documents link together

This is a small Quarto **website**. `index.qmd` (this page) is the master
document; everything else lives in `docs/` and the navbar ties them into a
narrative:

```
Home (index) → EDA → Models {XGBoost, RF, Neural Net, Elastic Net, SVM, MARS} → Stack → Submission → Kaggle Setup
```

- **[Exploratory Data Analysis](docs/01-eda.qmd)** — look at the data, find the
  patterns (quality, size, neighborhood, age, the log-price transform, the "NA
  means absent" gotcha), and *motivate* the feature engineering.
- **Model docs** — each follows the *same* structure (recipe → spec → workflow →
  tune → finalize → evaluate → save), so once you've read one, the others are
  easy to skim.
- **[Submission](docs/submission.qmd)** — a single *parameterized* document that
  turns any saved model into a leaderboard-ready CSV.
- **[Kaggle Setup](docs/setup-kaggle.md)** — authenticate the Kaggle CLI.

## Project structure

```
house-prices/
├── _quarto.yml              # website config (theme, navbar, freeze, pre-render)
├── index.qmd                # ← you are here (master document)
├── renv.lock                # pinned package versions (reproducibility)
├── R/
│   ├── 00_setup.R           # libraries, seed=42, paths, parallel backend
│   ├── 01_eda.R             # standalone EDA script
│   ├── 02_features.R        # make_recipe(data) — the SHARED feature recipe
│   └── 03_engineer.R        # NA→None/0 recoding + derived features (pre-render)
├── data/
│   ├── raw/                 # train.csv, test.csv, sample_submission.csv, data_description.txt
│   └── processed/           # engineered train.csv / test.csv (built by 03_engineer.R)
├── docs/
│   ├── 01-eda.qmd           # exploratory analysis
│   ├── 02-xgboost.qmd       # boosted trees
│   ├── 03-random-forest.qmd # ranger random forest
│   ├── 04-neural-net.qmd    # nnet MLP
│   ├── 06-elasticnet.qmd    # glmnet penalised linear
│   ├── 07-svm.qmd           # kernlab RBF SVM
│   ├── 08-mars.qmd          # earth MARS
│   ├── 05-stack.qmd         # stacked ensemble
│   ├── submission.qmd       # parameterized: build a submission CSV
│   └── setup-kaggle.md      # Kaggle CLI auth guide
├── models/                  # fitted workflows (*_fit.rds), tuning (*_res.rds), submission_*.csv
└── figures/                 # exported plots
```

The two shared pieces are **`R/03_engineer.R`** (deterministic up-front
engineering) and **`R/02_features.R`** (`make_recipe()`). Every model sources the
recipe so they all train on the *same* engineered features — that is what makes
the comparison fair.

## How to reproduce

Everything is pinned with [`renv`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) and uses
`here::here()` for paths, so there is no `setwd()` fragility.

1. **Restore the environment:**

   ```r
   renv::restore()
   ```

2. **Get the data** — the CSVs ship in `data/raw/`; or follow
   [the Kaggle setup guide](docs/setup-kaggle.md) to pull the official files.

3. **Render the site.** Because of `freeze: auto`, the heavy model fits only run
   the first time (or when a model doc changes):

   ```bash
   quarto render
   ```

   Logical run order: EDA → each base model doc (each saves its tuning result
   and fitted workflow to `models/`) → stack → submission.

::: {.callout-note}
`set.seed(42)` is set in `R/00_setup.R` and the resampling folds are seeded, so
CV results are reproducible across machines that share the `renv` lockfile.
:::

## Results summary

The table below compares the six base models on **cross-validated** `rmse` and
`rsq`, read **directly** from each model's saved tuning results
(`models/*_res.rds`), so they update automatically on every render. No copying.
The `rmse` is on the **log(SalePrice)** scale — the same units as the Kaggle
leaderboard.

```{r}
#| label: results-summary
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(here)

# Pull the best (rmse-selected) configuration's CV metrics from a saved
# tune_grid result.
cv_metrics <- function(path, label, notes) {
  res  <- readRDS(path)
  best <- select_best(res, metric = "rmse")
  m    <- collect_metrics(res) |> semi_join(best, by = names(best))
  tibble(
    Model           = label,
    `CV RMSE (log)` = m$mean[m$.metric == "rmse"],
    `CV R-squared`  = m$mean[m$.metric == "rsq"],
    `Best num_comp` = best$num_comp,
    Notes           = notes
  )
}

bind_rows(
  cv_metrics(here("models", "xgboost_res.rds"), "XGBoost",
             "tuned trees / tree_depth / learn_rate / min_n + num_comp"),
  cv_metrics(here("models", "rf_res.rds"), "Random Forest",
             "tuned mtry / min_n + num_comp; 1000 trees"),
  cv_metrics(here("models", "nnet_res.rds"), "Neural Net",
             "tuned hidden_units / penalty + num_comp; PCA-normalized"),
  cv_metrics(here("models", "elasticnet_res.rds"), "Elastic Net",
             "glmnet: tuned penalty / mixture + num_comp"),
  cv_metrics(here("models", "svm_res.rds"), "SVM (RBF)",
             "kernlab: tuned cost / rbf_sigma + num_comp"),
  cv_metrics(here("models", "mars_res.rds"), "MARS",
             "earth: tuned num_terms / prod_degree + num_comp")
) |>
  arrange(`CV RMSE (log)`) |>
  mutate(across(c(`CV RMSE (log)`, `CV R-squared`), \(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrl")
```

The [stacked ensemble](docs/05-stack.qmd) blends all six; its real test is the
Kaggle leaderboard rather than a single CV number.

## The submission workflow at a glance

Once a model is fitted and saved (each model doc does this), turning it into a
leaderboard entry is mechanical and wrapped in the **[parameterized submission
document](docs/submission.qmd)**:

```bash
quarto render docs/submission.qmd -P model:xgboost
quarto render docs/submission.qmd -P model:stack
```

That loads `models/<model>_fit.rds`, predicts on the test set, **exponentiates**
the log predictions back to dollars, writes `models/submission_<model>.csv`
(`Id`, `SalePrice`), and prints the exact `kaggle competitions submit` command.
